business_summary.text: India Glycols Limited is a diversified conglomerate with businesses in chemicals, potable spirits, bio-fuels, and bio-pharma. The company is undergoing a demerger to segregate these into three dedicated entities.

call_points.text: IGL Spirits targets EBITDA in excess of ₹500 Cr for FY27, with aspirations to become debt-free from FY28
Incremental capex of ₹5-10 Cr expected for FY27, with modular expansion planned as businesses grow
Debt reduction has supported profitable growth, with debt-to-equity ratio improving
JV performance improved with net revenue up 21% QoQ, driven by reduced disadvantage in ethylene oxide pricing
No specific FY27 revenue or margin guidance provided, management focused on sustaining margin expansion
Bio-Fuels segment to benefit from potential ethanol blending increase beyond 20% and flexi vehicles
Debt reduction continues with ₹268 Cr normal liability for FY27 plus additional prepayments planned
Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure, expected to recover through customer diversification

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company vide its Letter dated 9th April,2024 has informed that the Company has received an Order from Additional Commissioner, Noida Customs Commissionerate, Uttar Pradesh, dated 22nd March, 2024 (received on 9th April, 2024) demanding an amount of Rs. 33.43 Crore as duty short paid along with applicable interest and imposing penalty of Rs. 82 Crore under the Customs Act, 1962. In the same order, redemption fine of Rs.191.76 Crore was also imposed on the goods already cleared during the period from 1st July 2017 to 1st February 2021. Thereafter, an appeal against the said order was filed on7th June 2024, before the Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), GST Bhawan, Sector-48, Noida.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner Of Customs, Noida Customs Commissionerate

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Commissioner has filed an appeal challenging the order passed by the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi (“CESTAT”), New Delhi, setting aside the Commissioner’s earlier order dated 9th May 2019. The Company has not yet received a notice from the Hon’ble High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital but was informed by its consultant after the matter appeared on the Court’s website. The matter pertains to the classification of 'RAB' under the Central Excise Tariff for the financial years 2005 to 2009. The CESTAT has already adjudicated in favor of the Company against the order of the Commissioner. Central Excise Duty amounting to Rs.10,39,32,564/- along with applicable interest and penalty. As the Company has already been awarded a favorable order on this matter by CESTAT, hence the Company, post discussions with the experts, believes that the above demand is not maintainable.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, E-Block, Nehru Colony, Haridwar Road, Dehradun, Uttarakhand (Commissioner).

penalties.impact: Based on the Company’s assessment and advice of the legal counsel, the Company has a strong case on merit and will file the second appeal against such demand of duty, interest and penalty confirmed by the Appellate Authority and does not reasonably anticipate any material impact on its financial or operational or other activities.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A Show Cause notice was issued by Principal Commissioner alleging incorrect availment of Basic Customs Duty @2.5% instead of 5% during 01.07.2017 to 01.02.2021 on Import of DEA. Upon hearing, the Additional Commissioner had vide Order-in-Original dated 23.03.2024 confirmed an amount of Rs. 33.43 crore as duty paid short along with applicable interest, imposing penalty of Rs. 82 crore and redemption fine of Rs. 191.76 crore under the Customs Act, 1962. Subsequently, the Company filed an appeal before Commissioner (Appeals), Noida, Uttar Pradesh (“Appellate Authority”) against the Impugned Order-in-Original dated 23.03.2024. The Appellate Authority vide its Order-in-Appeal dated 27.02.2026 has partially allowed the Company's appeal and upheld the Impugned Order with respect to demand of Rs. 33.43 crore as duty short paid along with applicable interest and penalty of Rs. 41 crores.The demand for penalty amount of Rs. 41 crore and redemption fine of Rs. 191.76 crore had been set aside. Consequently, there has been a reduction in the substantial amount of total demand against the Company in this matter. Based on the Company’s assessment and advice of the legal counsel, the Company has a strong case on merit and is in process of filing appeal CESTAT, Allahabad against Order-in-Appeal dated 27.02.2026.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner of Customs, Noida Custom Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: The Company is in process of filling an appeal against the Order of the Appellate Authority.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had taken an Insurance Policy covering property damage, machinery breakdown, and consequential business interruption across its plant locations. In 2020, a claim was filed in respect of damaged machinery/equipment at the Kashipur Plant, which was rejected by the Insurance Company despite subsequent representations and submission of requisite documents/information for re-assessment. The claim was repudiated by the Insurance Company on more than one occasion. Based on internal assessment and legal opinion, the Company has initiated steps to challenge the said repudiation before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court for recovery of a claim of Rs. 79.76 Crore (Rupees Seventy-Nine Crore Seventy Six Lakh) towards material damage and loss of profit, along with interest and therefore, had filed an application on 21st May, 2026 for Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement under the applicable laws.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The New India Assurance Co. Limited (“Insurance Company”).

operating_notes.text: Grain prices stable at ₹21-22 per kilo, with increasing use of maize (46% of ethanol production)

Silver sale during shutdown generated ₹98 Cr revenue (purchase price ₹51 Cr)
IMFL volume grew 55% YoY to 1.4 million cases, with Prestige & Above segment doubling to 0.5 million cases

Nicotine sales grew two times QoQ driven by customer conversions in Europe and capacity expansion at Kashipur plant
